landing.heroTitle: Action Board, sports video analysis platform
landing.heroDescription: Action Board helps coaches, clubs, video analysts and students structure observations with analysis panels, a clear timeline, statistics and saved online resources.

sections.accessibleTitle: Make sports video analysis more accessible
sections.accessibleText: Video analysis should not be reserved for professional structures. Action Board provides a progressive, educational way to observe video, qualify important actions and prepare more useful feedback for athletes.
sections.panelsText: An analysis panel groups event, label and stats buttons. You can adapt it to your sport, working method or a specific training goal.
sections.timelineTitle: Analyze videos with a structured timeline
sections.timelineText: The timeline helps you find important moments, visualize occurrences and connect observations to the video. Timelines are private and visible only to their owner.
sections.saveText: Panels and timelines can be saved so you can retrieve your work. Panels can be private or public, while timelines cannot be public. Import/export also helps reuse or share an analysis structure.
sections.statsText: Stats buttons let you track indicators during video analysis based on configured events and labels.
sections.privacyText: When an account is deleted, private resources are removed according to the existing logic. Public panels may be kept in anonymized form to preserve resources shared with the community.
sections.freeTitle: A free platform with an account
sections.freeText: Action Board is currently free for users with an account. The platform will continue to evolve and may later offer dedicated plans for clubs, teams or organizations.

features.title: Action Board features
features.description: Discover sports video analysis, custom panels, the timeline, keyboard shortcuts, statistics, online saving and imports/exports available in Action Board.

pricing.title: Action Board is currently free with an account
pricing.intro: The platform is in active development and continuous improvement. You can create a free account to use analysis panels, the timeline and available saving tools.
pricing.freeTitle: A free base to democratize sports video analysis
pricing.freeText: Action Board first aims to make sports video analysis more accessible to amateur coaches, clubs, independent analysts and students. Current access lets you test essential workflows without a subscription.
pricing.futureText: Dedicated offers for clubs, teams or organizations may be proposed later once support, storage and collaboration needs are better stabilized.

legal.termsIntro: This page presents the current general usage charter for Action Board. It is temporary and may be expanded with a more detailed legal version.
legal.temporaryText: These terms of use are a temporary version intended to frame current platform usage. They may later be completed or replaced by a detailed legal version.
legal.purposeText: Action Board is a sports video analysis platform. It lets users create and use analysis panels, work with a timeline, save resources online and import or export panels and timelines.
legal.accountText: The user is responsible for the information provided when creating an account. In this platform version, users may choose to use a dedicated or temporary email address. Using a real personal email address remains their own choice and responsibility.
legal.dataText: Timelines are private. Panels may be private or public. Public panels are intended to be viewed or reused by logged-in users, depending on the available features.
legal.deletionText: Deleting an account removes private analyses and panels according to the existing logic. Public panels may be kept in anonymized form to preserve resources shared with the community.

privacy.title: Temporary Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This privacy policy is a temporary version describing how the platform currently works. It may be completed later.
privacy.accountText: Creating an account links panels, timelines and private resources to a user. Authentication protects application routes and restores saved work.
privacy.timelinesText: Timelines are private. Public timelines are not available in the current Action Board behavior. They are visible only to their owner.
privacy.panelsText: Panels may be private or public. Public panels may be visible to logged-in users to make analysis resources easier to reuse.
privacy.deletionText: Private panels and private analyses are deleted when the account is removed according to the existing logic. Public panels may be kept in anonymized form after account deletion.
privacy.cookiesText: The application uses authentication and may rely on cookies or session information depending on the current technical configuration. These elements maintain the user session and secure access to logged-in features.

videoShortcuts.title: Video shortcuts cheatsheet
videoShortcuts.miniDescription: The reserved video shortcuts actually configured in the hotkey service.
videoShortcuts.intro: These shortcuts come from the existing hotkey service configuration and help control the video during analysis.

paragraphs.0: They help you stay focused on observation, return precisely to an action and adjust speed without leaving the keyboard.

videoAnalysis.title: How does video analysis work?
videoAnalysis.miniDescription: The three main elements: analysis panel, video and timeline.
videoAnalysis.intro: Video analysis in Action Board relies on three complementary elements: the analysis panel, the video and the timeline.

bullets.0: Analysis panel: groups the buttons that trigger or qualify observations.
bullets.1: Video: can be controlled with shortcuts and playback controls.
bullets.2: Timeline: structures occurrences created during analysis so important moments can be found again.

paragraphs.0: During playback, the user can control the video, trigger analysis buttons and produce structured information in the timeline.

analysisPanel.title: How does an analysis panel work?
analysisPanel.miniDescription: Understand event, label and stats buttons in a custom panel.
analysisPanel.intro: A custom analysis panel speeds up observation by grouping the actions useful to your workflow.

bullets.0: Event: generates occurrences in the timeline.
bullets.1: Label: defines or qualifies an occurrence.

paragraphs.0: Hotkeys and activation links make repetitive actions faster to trigger. A panel adapted to your sport can reduce time spent searching, qualifying and counting important situations.
paragraphs.1: Public panels can be reused by other logged-in users. Detailed documentation may be added later.

saveShare.title: How do I save my analyses and panels?
saveShare.miniDescription: Online saving, panel visibility and timeline privacy.
saveShare.intro: Action Board lets you find your work online through panel and timeline saving, plus import/export.

bullets.0: A panel can be saved online.
bullets.1: A panel can be private or public.
bullets.2: Public panels are visible only to logged-in users.
bullets.3: Panels can be imported or exported.

bullets.0: A saved timeline always remains private.
bullets.2: Timelines can be imported or exported.
bullets.3: Timelines are visible only to their owner.

projectGoal.title: Why this project exists
projectGoal.miniDescription: Simpler video analysis for every sports profile.
projectGoal.intro: Our goal is simple: make video analysis accessible and useful every day, without unnecessary complexity.

bullets.0: Observe key moments of a match or training session faster.
bullets.1: Share clear feedback with staff and players.
bullets.2: Save time between preparation, observation and follow-up.

uxWorkflow.title: How the interface works
uxWorkflow.miniDescription: Easily identify pending, saved and editable data.
uxWorkflow.intro: The home area is organized to help you quickly find the right information at the right time.

bullets.0: Pending data: information linked to the current page, ready to display.
bullets.1: Saved data: items kept so you can find them later in one click.
bullets.2: Edit mode: customize the display to match how you work.

analysisOverview.title: Discover the Analysis page
analysisOverview.miniDescription: Video, timeline and sequencer work together to guide your analysis.
analysisOverview.intro: The Analysis page is your main workspace for reviewing an action, annotating and tracking sequences.

bullets.0: Login required: your settings and markers stay linked to your account.
bullets.1: Video component: control playback and return precisely to each phase.
bullets.2: Timeline: visualize match flow and important moments.
bullets.3: Sequencing panel: classify and trigger your analysis actions quickly.

legacyVideoShortcuts.title: Default video shortcuts
legacyVideoShortcuts.miniDescription: Control playback and video exploration without leaving the keyboard.
legacyVideoShortcuts.intro: These shortcuts let you analyze an action without breaking concentration or losing time in menus.

bullets.0: Quick play / pause to stop at exactly the right moment.
bullets.1: More precise navigation to return to a key sequence in seconds.
bullets.2: Frame-by-frame analysis to check a technical or tactical detail.
bullets.3: Slow motion and speed changes to better read movement and timing.

benefits.heading: What the video component brings you

paragraphs.0: You can review the same action several times, compare two passages and validate your observation more calmly.
paragraphs.1: The goal is simple: provide a smooth analysis experience, even during a quick debrief after a match or training session.

paragraphs.0: The player is designed to remain compatible with common video workflows, so you can start quickly without complicating your routine.

sequencerOverview.title: Understand the sequencing panel
sequencerOverview.miniDescription: Structure your events and labels to keep a clear view of the match.
sequencerOverview.intro: The sequencing panel helps you organize markers and analyze methodically, during the action and later during review.

bullets.0: Event: an important moment you want to identify, such as a shot, recovery or turnover.
bullets.1: Label: a tag to qualify the action with an area, intention, result or context.
bullets.2: Stat: a summary to track trends and support decisions.

second.heading: Why it is useful in practice

bullets.0: During analysis, you capture information as the video runs without losing focus.
bullets.1: After analysis, you quickly find key passages to prepare clear feedback for your group.
bullets.2: You save time comparing, prioritizing and sharing the points that really matter.

timelineOverview.title: Read the timeline efficiently
timelineOverview.miniDescription: Place each sequence in time to prepare targeted feedback.
timelineOverview.intro: The timeline gives you a clear chronological reading of the match or training session so you can find a passage instantly.

bullets.0: Visualize key moments in the order they happen.
bullets.1: Identify an important sequence and restart targeted playback.
bullets.2: Navigate easily through the analysis to compare several situations.
bullets.3: Select events to build a more structured debrief.

paragraphs.0: Instead of searching through the video for a long time, you access useful passages directly to explain, correct or highlight an action.
paragraphs.1: If navigation shortcuts are enabled, they make moving from one sequence to another even smoother.

items.question: What is Action Board?
items.answer: Action Board is a sports video analysis platform that helps create analysis panels, annotate video with a timeline and track statistics during observation.

items.question: Who is the platform for?
items.answer: The platform is for amateur coaches, amateur clubs, independent or club video analysts, and students.

items.question: Which sports are compatible?
items.answer: Action Board targets every sport. Panels can be adapted to a sport, team or analysis method.

items.question: Do I need to be logged in to use public panels?
items.answer: Yes. Public panels can be found and reused by logged-in users.

items.question: Can timelines be public?
items.answer: No. Timelines are private and visible only to their owner.
